page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 family, operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores via two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include a GPU, but it bundles 2,577 GB of integrated local SSD storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput. The instance scored 62,149.0 on stress-ng multi-core and achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,422.0, placing in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 291.88 GB/sec, alongside a write throughput of 134.9 GB/sec. Specialized computational tasks show high efficiency, including Geekbench clang software compilation at 42,333.0, PassMark database operations at 30,145.69, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 62.0 million operations per second. In contrast, single-thread metrics fall within the middle 50% average range, reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,649.0 and a single-core stress-ng rating of 1,899.49.

Hardware instruction flags include AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), and cryptographic accelerations (AES, VAES, and SHA_NI), supporting vector math and encrypted operations. While LLM inference throughput on CPU remains modest across 7B and 70B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators, the instance provides high density for multi-threaded server workloads. Cost efficiency is maximized when running heavily parallelized applications that fully utilize the 32 physical cores and high-capacity bundled SSD rather than relying strictly on single-thread clock speeds.

The D64d_v5 is well suited for high-throughput relational databases, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, enterprise software compilation pipelines, large-scale static web serving, and data transformation or ETL workloads requiring high local scratch capacity.
